title.narrative: Preservation of indigenous languages and ICH elements in the Peruvian Amazonian

description.narrative:
The project contributes to community initiatives by activating participatory strategies for the preservation and transmission of the Kukama-Kukamiria, Ikitu, and Taushiro indigenous languages located in the communities of San Jorge in the Nauta district, the San Antonio community in the Alto Nanay district, and the Intuto community in the Tigre district, Loreto region. These three languages represent means for transmitting endangered Indigenous knowledge and practices.
The project will implement a variety of strategies, such as workshops, training for youth and community leaders using technology, and the production of educational materials — all aimed at revitalizing Indigenous languages and ancestral knowledge. The strategy is led by more than 10 young people from the communities, reaching over 200 families.
Linguistic revitalization is crucial for preserving cultural identity, transmitting ancestral knowledge, and promoting the sustainable development of communities.
